Article Title: ‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
Article Text:
“So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,” Hasina said (Photo: Reuters).

Hasina alleges crackdown on Awami League members

Hasina raises concern over influence of extremist groups

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday reiterated her commitment to return to Dhaka in December despite a death sentence awaiting her return from India.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told The Associated Press in response to questions by email.“So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed,” Hasina said.The former leader has served as Prime Minister of Bangladesh for one term from 1996 to 2001 and four consecutive terms from 2009 to 2024.In 2024, Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government. In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal ordered her death sentence for crimes against humanity. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to the United Nations data, cited by AP, nearly 1,400 were killed during the unrest.The former PM has denied wrongdoing, rejected the tribunal's verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her. However, New Delhi said the request was being legally examined.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” India’s high commissioner to Dhaka Dinesh Trivedi remarked during an October discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.On Wednesday, Hasina told the AP that she was aware of the risks she could face on returning, but had no intention of changing her decision.“I know that I may be arrested when I return. I may be imprisoned, tortured or even killed. I am fully aware of those possibilities. But I cannot spend the rest of my life watching my people suffer from a distance,” she told the news agency.Hasina did not specify how she intended to travel back to Bangladesh from India.Her proposed return comes as her Awami League party faces an uncertain political future. The party remains banned, while several of its senior leaders have been arrested or forced into exile.Hasina alleged that at least 20,000 party members had been killed since August 2024. She also claimed that thousands had been arrested, tortured or driven into hiding, while supporters had lost their homes, businesses and livelihoods because of their political affiliations.“There is no normal political or democratic environment,” she said, accusing the authorities of systematically targeting the party.Following Hasina's removal from office, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus headed an interim administration for 18 months. In February, Tarique Rahman, son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia and a longstanding political rival of Hasina, won a landslide victory in an election held under the interim government. The Awami League was barred from contesting the polls.Several rights organisations, including Human Rights Watch, have criticised Rahman's government over alleged violations of civil and political rights in recent months. The government has maintained that arrests have been made in connection with specific charges.Hasina also expressed concern over the growing influence of hard-line groups in Bangladesh, saying the political climate had allowed extremist elements to gain confidence.“The present political environment has allowed extremist elements to become more confident,” she said.Global rights groups and independent observers had earlier raised concerns about radical groups seeking to suppress liberal forces during the Yunus-led interim administration. Minority communities have also reported facing intimidation.The interim government denied the allegations. The current administration has continued to face criticism over the deteriorating law and order situation in the country.Hasina, who took a tough stance against radical groups during her 15 years in power, said she was worried about their growing influence.Asked whether she expected countries such as the United States and India to press Bangladesh to ensure her safe return, Hasina said she was not seeking protection from foreign governments.“I value friendship and cooperation with all nations. That has always been our (Bangladesh's) foreign policy. But I do not need the blessing of a foreign power to return to my own country,” she said.
Article Summary: Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Dhaka in December. Hasina sought asylum in New Delhi after a mass student-led uprising overthrew her government. She was tried for ordering a crackdown that killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India to extradite her.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said the High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), constituted to investigate violence during student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in July, had received very few complaints from those affected by it.During the hearing, the panel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that it had issued notices in 149 newspapers inviting complaints regarding the violence during a march to Parliament on July 20. However, it received very few complaints, either online or in physical form.It also informed the top court that it had issued another appeal inviting complaints on October 21.Following this, the bench, also comprisig Justice Joymalya Bagchi, observed that in the absence of sufficient material, the panel was currently unable to arrive at any finding. It gave the committe one month to submit an initial fact-finding report.The bench also directed that all petitions, videos and complaints related to the violence be forwarded to the committee, which was constituted by the top court under the chairmanship of retired Supreme Court judge R Subhash Reddy.The other members of the panel include former Punjab and Haryana high court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Shalinder Kaur, ex-CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP LR Bishnoi.The Supreme Court had constituted the committe in August to investigate allegations of violence against student protesters and police personnel during demonstrations at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country.The protests were organised to demand the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET-UG paper leak in May. Jantar Mantar, Delhi's designated protest site at the time, emerged as the focal point of the demonstrations, which later spread to other parts of the country.Pradhan resigned on July 25, following which the protests came to an end.
Article Summary: The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) was constituted to investigate violence during student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in July. The panel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that it had issued notices in 149 newspapers inviting complaints. However, it received very few complaints, either online or in physical form.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Youth Congress has suspended more than 200 office-bearers across seven states for failing to participate in the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1.The disciplinary action comes days after several opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, attended the rally, where they accused the BJP and the Election Commission of undermining democratic institutions through alleged “vote chori”.The rally, which also saw opposition parties protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, was attended by senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, who demanded Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.Addressing the gathering, Rahul Gandhi alleged that the CEC had helped the BJP manipulate elections and warned that legal action would follow. “Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner. NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that it is considering constituting a committee to revisit the University Grants Commission 's (UGC) notified rules introduced to prevent caste discrimination in educational institutions, Bar and Bench reported.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the Centre is examining the issue to address students' concerns and ensure that no section feels dissatisfied or apprehensive."The government has taken a decision that every student should be taken care of. Nobody should have any apprehension. Nobody should feel dissatisfied. We are also considering the interests of the younger generation. The government is contemplating appointing a committee," SG Mehta told the apex court.This comes as the apex court was hearing a batch of petitions challenging the UGC regulations.The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the top court on January 29.At the time, the court said the provisions were "prima facie vague" and could have "very sweeping consequences", warning that they could potentially divide society and have a "dangerous impact".The court had also asked the Centre and the UGC to respond to three petitions challenging the new framework."In exercise of our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we further direct that the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2012, will continue to operate and remain in force till further orders," it had said.The regulations had faced opposition in several places, with student groups and other organisations calling for their immediate withdrawal.

Article Title: EC announces electoral roll revision in 6 states, UTs; final rolls on Jan 21

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday announced a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories, including Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim.The exercise aims to ensure that all eligible citizens are enrolled in the electoral rolls, with a particular focus on young and first-time voters. It will also facilitate advance applications from individuals who will turn 18 and become eligible to vote on April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2027.According to the schedule announced by the Commission, the draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30, while the final rolls are scheduled to be released on January 21, 2027.The Commission has directed the chief secretaries of the respective states and Union territories to ensure that adequate manpower and resources are made available to complete the exercise.The latest announcement comes months after the poll body unveiled Phase 3 of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in May. The third phase covered 16 states and three Union territories, including Delhi, Chandigarh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.The SIR exercise was aimed at verifying the eligibility of around 36.7 crore electors and was scheduled to be conducted in phases, with the Commission taking into account the Census 2027 schedule and the availability of common field-level staff involved in both exercises.
Article Summary: The Election Commission announced a Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in six states and Union territories. The exercise aims to ensure that all eligible citizens are enrolled in the electoral rolls, with a particular focus on young and first-time voters. The draft electoral rolls will be published on November 30, while the final rolls are scheduled to be released on January 21, 2027.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before the Delhi Police Crime Branch on Thursday in connection with the October 13 Jantar Mantar protest, which led to their detention on charges of trespassing at the denotified protest site.The two CJP leaders reached the Crime Branch office in Rajouri Garden after being summoned to join the investigation. Fellow leader Ajinkya Shinde was also summoned in the case.Das, Ranka and Shinde had earlier skipped questioning scheduled for October 22. Ranka had said they could not appear on the scheduled date and had informed the police about their inability to attend. The leaders were awaiting fresh dates for questioning, he had said."We are waiting to hear from them. We have not received a specific date yet. We could not make it on the previous date, and we had informed them about that. They said they would confirm the timings, so we are waiting for the Crime Branch to get back to us," Ranka had said.The police had detained Das and Ranka following the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site. According to the police, the leaders entered the area through private premises and violated conditions imposed to maintain peace.The two CJP leaders were released from judicial custody on October 21 by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court after furnishing personal and surety bonds and submitting written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.In their undertakings, Das and Ranka promised not to breach peace or disturb public tranquillity. They also agreed not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar until the site is denotified in accordance with the law, and said any future demonstrations would be held within the constitutional framework.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka appeared before the Delhi Police Crime Branch on Thursday. They were detained on charges of trespassing at the denotified protest site. Fellow leader Ajinkya Shinde was also summoned in the case.

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , listing seven conditions that he said the opposition party should follow if it wants to "win more MPs".In a post on X, Rijiju said Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" and stop promoting their agenda. He also urged the Congress leader to respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, saying it was part of Indian tradition.Listing the conditions, Rijiju asked Gandhi to "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently."He further advised him to "end deep hatred against BJP, RSS and Modi Ji" and "treat BJP as political opponent, not enemy."The minister also asked Gandhi to take "Parliament more seriously" and allow MPs to participate in debates and discussions."Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he said, listing the final two conditions.Rijiju's remarks came amid an ongoing exchange between the ruling BJP and the Congress over Rahul Gandhi's demand for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Earlier on Wednesday, Rijiju shared a video clip of his speech in Parliament during which opposition leaders had walked out of the House."Parliament is the House for debates & discussion. But people who don't believe in democracy, debates and discussion are talking about debate," the parliamentary affairs minister said.Meanwhile, Rahul renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate, claiming that he could establish within five minutes that the prime minister was a traitor. His remarks drew a sharp response from Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.Following Rahul's challenge, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged the prime minister to come forward and answer questions raised over alleged vote theft.In a post on X, Kharge said Modi had no answers on the "vote chori" issue and should accept Gandhi's challenge to debate various subjects, including "foreign connections"."You don't come to Parliament. You have not done a SINGLE OPEN PRESS CONFERENCE; it's time you came for a DEBATE.“Come forward, Face Questions. Tell the Nation why did you indulge in VOTE CHORI !!” Kharge said.“PM Modi is parroting his flop line of ‘Dimaagi Naxal’! He has NO answer on Vote Chori and the Open Challenge by Rahul Gandhi to discuss how he mortgaged Indian interests to Foreign powers!” he added.Kharge also questioned Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks about three crore voters being "ghuspaithiyas" (infiltrators), asking what he had been doing as home minister if illegal immigrants had entered the country.“He should be sacked for his incompetence,” the Congress president said.Responding to Rahul's challenge, Sitharaman said Parliament was already an appropriate venue for a debate and reminded him that he was the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha."Rahul ji, you ask the Prime Minister to choose a venue for a debate. There is already one: Parliament, where you happen to be the LoP."Just yesterday, Home Minister Shri Amit Shah offered a special session to debate SIR and EVMs. Why not show the same enthusiasm for a debate in Parliament that you show while issuing challenges on social media?" Sitharaman said on X.She said that demanding answers also required Rahul to stay and hear the government's response."Demanding answers also carries an obligation to hear them," she said, alleging that Gandhi and other Congress leaders had walked out of Parliament on several occasions while the government was responding to their allegations.Sitharaman also accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies of repeatedly disrupting parliamentary proceedings, resulting in entire sittings being washed out.She further questioned the nature of Gandhi's allegations and asked him to present specific claims backed by evidence."Simply throwing together a long list of accusations doesn’t make your case any stronger. As LoP, you are expected to show some seriousness and responsibility."You say, 'Daro mat'. Then bring the facts, face the scrutiny and stay to hear the answers. In the House, uphold the standards of debate you demand from others," she said.

NEW DELHI: Ravi Uppal, a prime accused in the multi-crore Mahadev online betting case, has been arrested in Dubai. The development comes days after co-accused Sourabh Chandrakar was extradited to India from Oman. Enforcement authorities have formally moved for Uppal's extradition, and sources said he is likely to be handed over soon to stand trial in India.Uppal was detained on the basis of an extradition request from India, with the CBI and ED establishing his last known location in the UAE.Uppal had briefly left the UAE for Vanuatu and acquired citizenship of the Pacific nation but failed to get his name removed from Interpol's Red Notice as the ED had opposed his plea before the Interpol Commission for Control of Files.He was arrested by Dubai police in Dec 2023 and was under house arrest but was released in Nov 2025 despite an extradition request pending since 2023. India has an extradition treaty with the UAE, and the Gulf nation had extradited high-profile accused in the past, including British national Christian Michel, wanted in the AgustaWestland VVIP chopper scam.India had sent a formal extradition request after Dubai police informed New Delhi of his arrest.However, the UAE authorities later said no extradition request had been received and released the accused. Indian agencies again located him in Dubai in May this year, and efforts were under way to bring him back.Uppal and other co-accused, including Chandrakar, had launched the Mahadev app in 2019 and managed to expand the user base significantly during the Covid pandemic. Uppal played a key role in orchestrating the gambling network by franchising thousands of branches across India and abroad on a profit-sharing basis.
Article Summary: Ravi Uppal, prime accused in the multi-crore Mahadev online betting case, has been arrested in Dubai. Enforcement authorities have formally moved for his extradition. Sources said he is likely to be handed over soon to stand trial in India.

NEW DELHI: Delhi's air quality remained in the severe category on Thursday morning, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 482 at 8.01am. Several parts of the national capital continued to record high pollution levels.According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data, seven monitoring stations recorded AQI levels above 400, falling in the severe category.Punjabi Bagh recorded the highest AQI at 446, followed by Narela at 434, Rohini at 431, RK Puram at 416, Bawana at 412, North Campus, Delhi University, at 408 and Patparganj at 405.Several other areas reported very poor air quality. Okhla Phase-2 and India Gate both recorded an AQI of 399, followed by ITO at 397, Dwarka Sector 8 at 396, Chandni Chowk at 356 and Vasundhara Enclave at 330.Anand Vihar recorded an AQI of 293, while the IMD Lodhi Road station reported 268. Both stations fell in the poor category.Amid the deterioration in Delhi's air quality, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said on Tuesday that the Centre's air quality panel was continuously monitoring meteorological conditions, including wind direction, wind speed and the movement of air. He also assured that necessary action was being taken.The worsening air quality comes despite a decline in stubble-burning incidents compared to previous years. The government has claimed that a significant portion of paddy stubble has been utilised through ex-situ management.Asked about the reduction in stubble-burning incidents in neighbouring states, including Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, Yadav said, “Yes, I have already stated that around 40 per cent of the paddy stubble has been utilised through ex-situ management this time."Responding to reporter’s question on why air quality continues to remain in the severe category despite these measures, Yadav said the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) was closely monitoring meteorological conditions and taking necessary steps based on its assessments.“CAQM is continuously monitoring meteorological conditions, including wind direction, wind speed and the movement of air. Based on these assessments, the necessary steps are being taken,” he said.Dr Saurabh Mittal, Assistant Professor in the Department of Pulmonary, Critical Care and Sleep Medicine at AIIMS, Delhi, said, "Since AQI has increased, we are seeing patients who have prior respiratory problems, but now they are coming with increased symptoms and exacerbations, for which we need to increase their medications, like their inhaler doses have to be increased, and some patients need the addition of new medications such as oral steroids also to reduce their cough. We are also seeing patients who have previously been asymptomatic, but now, because of the increased pollution, they are developing respiratory symptoms in terms of cough, irritation of the throat, nasal irritation, and shortness of breath. So those patients also need some kind of treatment or decongestants for symptom relief... There has been an increase in people actually calling us... I would say that we anticipate that this number is probably going to increase in the next couple of weeks..."Explaining the factors contributing to the pollution, Mittal said, "It's a multifactorial problem. It's not a one-time or one-day problem. Of course, weather contributes significantly to it; as the winter weather appears, the condensation happens. Of course, vehicular emissions, construction, stubble burning - all of these things contribute to a larger extent. But individual contribution is very difficult to kind of quantify. But yes, if we reduce all of them, it's likely that we'll have some relief from the problem."
Article Summary: Delhi's air quality remained in the severe category on Thursday morning. The overall Air Quality Index (AQI) touched 482 at 8.01am. Seven monitoring stations recorded AQI levels above 400. The worsening air quality comes despite a decline in stubble-burning incidents.

Article Title: 24-hour arrest clock starts from detention, not formal arrest: Supreme Court
Article Text:
'No artificial distinction': SC says 24-hour arrest clock starts from detention

The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour period within which an accused person must be produced before a judicial magistrate begins from the time of detention, and not merely from the time of formal arrest.The court held that arrest and detention are effectively the same for the purpose of this constitutional safeguard, as a person's liberty is curtailed in both situations.It observed that “any attempt to draw an artificial distinction between detention and arrest is constitutionally unsustainable”.The Supreme Court also criticised several high courts for making an artificial distinction between arrest and detention. It clarified that the requirement to produce an accused person before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours applies from the point at which the person is first detained.In another significant observation, the court ruled that the fundamental rights of an accused person must take precedence over provisions of special laws in cases involving delays in trial and the grant of bail. Referring to contradictory verdicts on bail in cases under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the court said the constitutional rights of an accused must be given priority.The court further observed that special laws cannot serve as a guide to interpreting the Constitution. Rather, such laws must be interpreted in accordance with constitutional principles.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that 24-hour period within which an accused person must be produced before a judicial magistrate begins from the time of detention. Article Title: Trump’s ‘Freedom In Space’ signals new contest for Moon; India’s challenge is safeguarding strategic autonomy
Article Text:
Trump's space declaration sparks a new Moon rules contest, forcing India to balance Artemis ties and 2047 ambitions against strategic autonomy.

Competing frameworks, competing interests

India’s strategic dilemma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: As Americans voted in the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation titled “The American Declaration of Freedom in Space”, declaring that the US would lead the exploration, development, use and settlement of space.Promising a return to the Moon by 2028, a permanent American lunar presence and an eventual human mission to Mars, the proclamation links space leadership directly to economic prosperity and national security.But beneath its rhetoric of freedom and exploration lies a larger geopolitical question: who will set the rules for humanity’s expansion beyond Earth, and will space remain a global commons or become an arena of competing national interests? For India, which has its own ambitions for human spaceflight and lunar exploration, the declaration brings this question into sharper focus.Susmita Mohanty, director general of space think tank Spaceport SARABHAI, says: “Trump describes space as ‘the province of all humans’ while, almost in the same breath, declaring his intention to establish a ‘permanent presence by American citizens’. The tension between these two assertions is difficult to ignore: a domain ostensibly belonging to all humanity is simultaneously being framed as a sphere for enduring American dominance,” she said.She also questioned the assertion of American superiority, pointing to the history of international contributions to space exploration. Russia, for instance, remained indispensable to American human spaceflight for nearly nine years after the retirement of the Space Shuttle fleet in 2011, transporting US astronauts to the International Space Station until SpaceX's Crew Dragon began crewed flights in 2020.Mohanty also pointed to China’s growing capabilities. Since 2007, China has completed six lunar missions, including two sample-return missions, and is working towards landing astronauts by 2030. “Space exploration has historically been a collaborative endeavour, one that repeatedly reminds terrestrial superpowers that their dominance has its limits,” she said.The implications extend beyond the US-China lunar race. Lt Gen AK Bhatt (retd), director-general of the Indian Space Association (ISpA), believes the proclamation signals a shift towards competing frameworks for governing space activities.“There’s now a clear divide of two groups: the Artemis-led group and the ILRS-led (China-Russia) group. Space colonisation, ownership and other things that have been talked about will definitely sow the seeds for future contests and maybe confrontation,” he said.The legal question is particularly important. Article I of the 1967 Outer Space Treaty describes space as the province of all mankind, while Article III prohibits national appropriation of celestial bodies. The proclamation, however, explicitly speaks of establishing a permanent American presence and developing resources, subject to international obligations. It does not itself confer ownership of lunar territory.India’s position is complicated by its participation in multiple international frameworks. It signed the Artemis Accords in June 2023, but also signed the 1979 Moon Agreement, which it has not ratified. The two frameworks have different approaches to aspects of lunar resource governance.In Aug 2026, Nasa invited Isro to join its Moon Base programme, building on the Artemis partnership. India, meanwhile, has its own Space Vision 2047, including the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and a human Moon landing by 2040.For Bhatt, this calls for a wider national debate on India's positioning. “The issue is basically where India aligns its cards. Though signing of the Artemis Accords was an indicator of our inclination, there has to be an internal debate within the Indian community,” he said.He also cautioned against dismissing the proclamation as political rhetoric. “It does not matter whether we take Donald Trump seriously or not. The signature on the paper is that of the President of the United States, aligning the policy for the future.”For India, the challenge may be to work with competing space powers without being confined to their geopolitical choices, while ensuring it has a say in the rules governing the next frontier.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump issued a proclamation titled ‘The American Declaration of Freedom in Space’ The proclamation promises a return to the Moon by 2028, a permanent American lunar presence and an eventual human mission to Mars. For India, which has its own ambitions for human spaceflight and lunar exploration, the declaration brings this question into sharper focus.

The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. Inviting Moosewala's father onto the stage, Rahul Gandhi recounted how the singer had walked into his office with tattoos and made an impression on him even before he had heard any of his songs. He also recalled feeling that Moosewala was entering a dangerous field when he decided to join politics.Rahul said he had not known much about Moosewala when they first met a few years ago. He had not heard his music or even his voice. However, the singer's personality and the impression he made during their interaction led Rahul to induct him into the Congress."A few years ago, I met his son at my office. At that time, I did not know Sidhu Moosewala. I was meeting him for the first time and did not know much about him. He was an impressive young man. He walked into the room with tattoos. I had not heard his songs or even his voice at that time. I was only told that he was a good person, a musician, and wanted to join the Congress party . As politicians, we observe people carefully when they come to meet us.We do not rely too much on their words; we go by our feelings and what our heart tells us about them. He was a dynamic and talented young man, so I inducted him into the party."Recalling the concern he felt during that meeting, the leader of opposition said he had sensed that Moosewala was stepping into a dangerous environment by entering politics. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party."During our meeting, a thought suddenly crossed my mind, though nobody had told me anything about it. I felt that he was entering a dangerous field. I don't know why I got that feeling. He was a singer, a dynamic young man, and someone who did not understand politics very well. I felt I should protect him in my own way. I did not mean physical protection; that thought had not even crossed my mind. I meant political protection. He was a young man entering politics, and I wanted him to feel comfortable in that environment."Moosewala was shot dead in May 2022 in Punjab's Mansa district. His killing had triggered widespread outrage and questions over the state's law-and-order situation.Rahul Gandhi had also invoked Moosewala's memory during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. When asked how many seats the INDIA bloc would win, he responded with a seemingly cryptic "295". The number was widely seen as a reference to Moosewala's popular song 295, adding another instance of the Congress leader's association with the late singer.Rahul Gandhi also targeted Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the drug problem in the state. Questioning the party's promise to eradicate drug abuse, he asked what parts of Punjab had been freed from the menace since the AAP came to power."The Aam Aadmi Party came to power, and you placed your trust in it. Punjab trusted Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party. What was their promise? That they would eradicate drug abuse. I want to ask you... Where have they eradicated drugs? From which part of Punjab have they managed to eliminate the drug menace? They cannot eradicate drugs."He also alleged that Mann's breath would smell of alcohol during their interactions in Parliament. Rahul said the chief minister would sit with MPs and crack jokes early in the morning, but that the smell of alcohol would be noticeable by 11am.Clarifying that he was not questioning Mann's personal choice to consume alcohol, Rahul said a chief minister leading a campaign against drug abuse could not himself be under the influence of intoxicants."Let me tell you another story about your chief minister. When I was in the Lok Sabha, he would sit with us early in the morning and crack jokes. However, by 11 am, his breath would smell of alcohol. I am not saying that Bhagwant Mann should not consume alcohol. That is his personal matter. If he wants to drink, it is his personal choice. But if you want to fight drug abuse, your chief minister cannot be under the influence of intoxicants every evening. "
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi fondly remembered late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala at the party's 'Insaaf Rally' The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party.

Article Title: Andhra, Kerala top ease of vehicle ownership index; UP, Bihar at bottom: Report
Article Text:
Representational image of a car showroom

NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu have emerged as the top-performing states in ease of vehicle ownership, while Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal rank at the bottom, reflecting wide disparities in procedures for transferring ownership of used vehicles.The findings are part of the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) 2026, prepared by Consumer Voice and Indiatech, which assessed systems and procedures across 15 major states and Delhi, covering more than 85% of India’s organised pre-owned vehicle market.None of the states figured in the ‘high ease’ or excellent category, with Andhra Pradesh, the highest-ranked state, scoring only 5.9 on a scale of 0-10. Kerala scored 5.7, followed by Tamil Nadu and Delhi at 4.6 each. Karnataka (4.3), Gujarat (4.2), Madhya Pradesh (4.1), Maharashtra and Telangana (4.1 each) and Punjab (4) occupied the next positions.Rajasthan (4) and Haryana (3.9) were also in the lower half of the rankings, while West Bengal (2.6), Bihar (2.5) and Uttar Pradesh (2.5) brought up the rear.The report comes as India’s pre-owned vehicle market is expanding rapidly and is projected to grow from $36.4 billion in 2025 to over $73.5 billion by 2030.The market has overtaken new vehicle sales in volume. However, fragmented state-level rules, incomplete digitisation and cumbersome procedures continue to impede seamless vehicle ownership transfers.The report, which also included interviews, found that 39% of citizens reported delays in receiving their registration certificates after completing vehicle transfers, while 61.5% were unaware of the requirement for a party-pusher until they reached the respective RTO.As many as 63% could not accurately estimate the total cost of completing an ownership transfer, reflecting widespread opacity in transaction charges.Interestingly, all respondents said they relied on intermediaries or agents to complete ownership transfers because of administrative complexity.The report has called for a unified digital vehicle records system, standardised no-objection certificate procedures, real-time integration between banks and transport departments for automatic removal of hypothecation after loan repayment, and transparent, time-bound service delivery across RTOs.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu have emerged as the top-performing states in ease of vehicle ownership. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal rank at the bottom. The findings are part of the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) 2026, prepared by Consumer Voice and Indiatech.

Ajit Pawar had appealed to Sharad Pawar to join the NDA, but he did not accept the offer," Athawale added, referring to Sharad Pawar's nephew Ajit Pawar, who died in a plane crash in January.In July 2023, Ajit Pawar split the then undivided NCP and joined the NDA. The Election Commission subsequently recognised Ajit's faction as the "real" NCP, while the Sharad Pawar-led faction was allotted the name Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar).At the time of Ajit Pawar's death, the two NCP factions were reportedly close to a merger, but the process was subsequently put on hold.Meanwhile, amid the ongoing debate over electronic voting machines (EVMs), Athawale expressed no objection to elections being conducted using ballot papers.Questioning the opposition's criticism of EVMs, he pointed out that the machines were not introduced by PM Modi.He further stated that if the NDA failed to win the 2029 general elections, it would congratulate Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and accept the people's "verdict ... without blaming EVMs".Athawale also expressed hope that drought-hit farmers in Maharashtra would receive financial assistance before Diwali.The Union minister further urged the Thane police to conduct an impartial probe into the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar, emphasising that no injustice should be done in the matter.
Article Summary: Union minister Ramdas Athawale claims Supriya Sule could get a berth in the Union Cabinet during its next expansion if her party joins the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) He also said that NCP chief Sharad Pawar, Sule's father, could have become President of India had he joined the ruling alliance in 2019.

Article Title: 'Dialled wrong number, season of dharna': CJI's quip at man seeking rotation of SC-ST reserved seats
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday quipped at a petitioner to organise public protests and demonstrations while rejecting his plea seeking mandatory rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Parliament and state assemblies.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana upheld the Allahabad high court order validating Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, which provides for the identification of reserved constituencies in areas where the proportion of SC/ST residents is comparatively high.The Supreme Court, however, said the petitioner was free to approach public representatives and persuade them to adopt the principle of rotation."You are dialling the wrong number. This is a season of dharna, protest etc. You should also do the same," Bar and Bench quoted CJI Surya Kant as saying in a lighter vein."This is also a good ground for protest," he added.During the hearing, Justice Bagchi said that in a multiparty democracy, voters are expected to make electoral choices based on political ideologies rather than caste or religious considerations."In a political democracy, there are multiple political parties having different ideologies.The voters are expected to vote for the party, not for the religion. You may like or dislike a particular political ideology. Who is representing that ideology becomes irrelevant. You vote for that ideology. So that also defeats your argument," Justice Bagchi said.The bench also distinguished between the right to vote and any claimed right to contest an election from a particular constituency. It observed that candidates belonging to the general category remain eligible to contest from constituencies that are not reserved.The petitioner, Jagdish Singh, had challenged the continued reservation of his constituency for Scheduled Castes, claiming that it had remained reserved for nearly seven decades since its creation.He argued that the absence of a rotation mechanism violated Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution and restricted voters' electoral choices by limiting the candidates they could elect to members of the SC community.He further claimed that the existing arrangement benefited a handful of political families rather than advancing the interests of the wider community.Seeking a mechanism similar to the rotational reservation provided for panchayats and municipalities under Articles 243D and 243T of the Constitution, the petitioner urged the bench to direct periodic rotation of SC/ST-reserved constituencies.Justice Bagchi, however, disagreed with the argument that candidates from the majority community would anyway get elected in constituencies with a high SC population, making reservation unnecessary."That proceeds on the idea that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. They may not vote on community and caste lines. The High Court cannot judicially pronounce on a democratic choice. That is for the voters to decide," Justice Bagchi said.The bench clarified that it could not rewrite the Constitution or the statute by introducing a rotation requirement that finds no mention in Articles 330 and 332 or the Delimitation Act.The Allahabad high court had held that Articles 330 and 332 merely prescribe the number of reserved seats in proportion to the population and leave the methodology for identifying reserved constituencies to Parliament under Article 327.It had found Section 9(1)(c) neither ultra vires nor violative of fundamental rights, ruling that courts cannot issue a mandamus directing the legislature to introduce a rotation provision.While acknowledging that rotation could better advance social and political justice by allowing SC/ST candidates to contest even from constituencies with smaller reserved-category populations, the high court had emphasised that the policy decision rests exclusively with Parliament.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant quipped at a petitioner to organise public protests and demonstrations. He rejected his plea seeking mandatory rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Parliament and state assemblies. The Supreme Court said the petitioner was free to approach public representatives and persuade them to adopt the principle of rotation.

Article Title: Centre proposes immediate suspension of licences for substandard drugs

NEW DELHI: A medicine that fails critical quality tests could soon trigger immediate suspension of the manufacturer’s licence, under proposed rules aimed at preventing substandard drugs from reaching patients. Health ministry has proposed changes to the drugs rules, 1945, to allow regulators to act without waiting for the existing show-cause notice process.Currently, authorities follow a procedure that includes issuing a show-cause notice before suspending or cancelling a manufacturing licence. This can create a gap during which medicines declared ‘Not of standard quality (NSQ)’ may continue to circulate.Under the proposed amendments, central or state drug licensing authority can immediately suspend manufacturing licence for a drug if a govt analyst’s report finds it deficient in any of five critical parameters: assay, dissolution, related substances, impurities or sterility.These tests determine whether a medicine contains the required amount of active ingredient, releases it properly in the body and is free from harmful impurities or microbial contamination.The suspension will continue until the manufacturer identifies the reason for the quality failure and takes corrective and preventive action. The licence can be restored only after the regulatory authority verifies that the required measures have been implemented.The ministry has also proposed a system to ensure that reports of substandard drugs reach the drugs controller general of India (DCGI), the state or UT drug licensing authority concerned, and the manufacturer and marketer. This is intended to speed up regulatory action and fix accountability across the supply chain.The draft amendments have been opened for public consultation.
Article Summary: The Health Ministry has introduced new regulations aimed at suspending manufacturing licenses for medicines that do not meet quality criteria. Currently, authorities follow a procedure that includes issuing a show-cause notice before suspending or cancelling a manufacturing licence. This can create a gap during which medicines declared ‘Not of standard quality’ may continue to circulate.

NEW DELHI: Changing NEET-PG and NEET-SS from a percentile-based to a rank-based system will not address the structural problems in medical education, doctors’ body said, flagging exorbitant fees, compulsory bonds, inadequate stipends and vacancies in less preferred specialities as the issues requiring urgent attention.“These were the key concerns raised by stakeholders at the October 9 DGHS meeting. Changing the merit-list methodology without addressing these issues is merely changing the approach, not reforming medical education,” United Doctors Front (UDF) chairperson Dr Lakshya Mittal who was part of the meeting said.The govt’s response to earlier stakeholder recommendations on these issues, reproduced in an expert committee report submitted to supreme court on Tuesday, points largely to state jurisdiction and existing regulations. On fee regulation, the govt cited NMC guidelines issued in February 2022 for determining charges for 50% of seats in private medical colleges and deemed universities, but said the guidelines were under litigation. Fee structures, it said, were governed by state regulatory authorities.On bonds, the govt said the policy fell under state jurisdiction. It also said stipends in National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences institutions were at par with those for MD/MS/DM/MCh seats in state institutions.Public-sector recruitment and job placements, it added, were also under state jurisdiction. These responses relate to earlier stakeholder recommendations and are not a direct reply to the October 9 meeting.At the meeting, Mittal had called for uniform fee regulation, bond-free admissions in pre-clinical and para-clinical branches, where seats often remain vacant, and equitable stipends. He also sought better faculty recruitment, career progression and research opportunities to address vacancies without resorting to zero or negative qualifying cut-offs.Other particpants in the meeting, Dr Raj Shekhar and Dr Ankit also flagged high fees, particularly in deemed universities, and sought fee regulatory committees to ensure reasonable charges. Participants called for uniform stipends across clinical and non-clinical branches and incentives for rural postings.Dr Nikhil questioned the basis for reducing qualifying percentiles in PG and super-speciality courses, including who took the decision and whether reductions should be restricted to the final counselling round. He also proposed independent audits of medical education costs.Participants cautioned against diluting qualifying standards merely to fill vacant seats. Dr G Raghavelu said measures to prevent seat wastage must protect professional standards. Biometric and KYC checks to prevent seat blocking were also suggested.The draft minutes record that qualifying marks could be reduced without compromising education quality, fees regulated uniformly through committees and stipends made more attractive. Separately, Supreme Court committee report records the NMC’s in-principle approval for a rank-based system for NEET-PG and NEET-SS, without declaring percentile marks. NEW DELHI: A dentist's degree does not automatically qualify them to perform every dental procedure. The National Dental Commission (NDC) has clarified that practitioners must restrict their clinical work to procedures covered by their qualifications and specialised training, bringing the scope of general and specialist dental practice into focus.In an advisory, the commission's Ethics and Dental Registration Board said it had received queries from registered dentists seeking clarity on the permissible scope of practice. It said the BDS and Master of Dental Surgery (MDS) curricula define the competencies and procedures that each category of dentist is trained to perform.The BDS curriculum covers routine procedures such as fillings, simple root canals, uncomplicated extractions, dentures and basic orthodontic treatment. Graduates are also expected to identify complex cases and refer them to specialists. MDS provides advanced training in fields such as oral surgery, orthodontics, periodontology, prosthodontics and endodontics.For instance, BDS graduates are trained in simple orthodontic procedures and routine extractions, while complex corrective jaw surgeries and advanced oral surgeries require specialist expertise.Welcoming the clarification, (Hony.) Brig Anil Kohli, former president of the Dental Council of India and an endodontist, said the NDC should issue a procedure-wise list defining the scope of general and specialist practice.“Routine procedures such as fillings, scaling, simple extractions and basic root canals can be performed by competent BDS graduates, but complex implants, impacted wisdom tooth surgeries, corrective jaw procedures and advanced periodontal treatments must be reserved for trained MDS specialists.The dividing line should be clinical competence, not just the degree, with patient safety taking precedence,” he said.Kohli also called for mandatory continuing dental education for licence renewal, backed by clinical audits and action against violations. General dentists with recognised additional training should be allowed to expand their scope of practice, he said.“Dentists must be transparent about their qualifications, expertise and limitations, explain treatment risks and refer patients when necessary. Ensuring appropriate treatment is their responsibility, not the patient’s. Patient interests must always come first,” he saidThe commission has asked state dental councils and tribunals to issue advisories or public notices clarifying the permitted scope of practice and preventing violations.
Article Summary: The National Dental Commission has clarified that practitioners must restrict their clinical work to procedures covered by their qualifications and specialised training. NEW DELHI: Dutch and Indian physicians and civil society organisations have come together to ensure access to a rare disease drug for seven children in India, by compounding the drug in the Hague and sending it to India. Compounding is the process by which a medicine is custom-made in small quantities.The drug, tiratricol, is going to be compounded by Transvaal Pharmacy for 1.8 euro per capsule, which is 99 times cheaper than the commercial drug sold by the Swedish company Egetis in Germany for 180 euro (over Rs 19,000) per tablet.Currently, the family of one of the children is importing the medicine from Germany. It costs them Rs 3 lakh per month. Since it is prescribed for life, buying it is proving to be unsustainable.The seven children suffer from a rare disease, Allan Herndon-Dudley Syndrome (AHDS), also known as MCT8 deficiency. Due to a genetic defect, their thyroid hormones are unable to reach their brain cells effectively, leading to severe developmental issues. Research by the Erasmus University Medical Centre (Erasmus MC) has confirmed that tiratricol, a medication known since 1953, could reduce the physical manifestations of the disease.Tiratricol has been in the market in France since 1974 to treat patients with thyroid conditions.In 2014, doctors at Erasmus MC, through research which involved 14 million euro of public funding, discovered that tiratricol could also be used to treat AHDS. Erasmus MC sold the intellectual property rights to Egetis without a “fair price clause”. In 2025, Egetis received European marketing authorisation for tiratricol, granting it 10 years of market exclusivity under the European orphan drug legislation. By 2026, the price per tablet of tiratricol had gone up from 0.35 euro, at which it was being sold in France in 2017, to almost 180 euro per tablet in Germany.The Netherland-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF) which works to ensure access to medicines and medical technologies in a sustainable manner, is coordinating the effort to make the drug available to children in India. Wilbert Bannenberg of PAF termed Egetis’ pricing of tiratricol an “unethical business model”.A news report on the funding effort, which caught the attention of PAF, kicked off the Dutch-India collaboration.Since compounding by a pharmacy is only an emergency fix, for a long-term solution PAF is working with access to medicine activists and paediatricians in India for affordable production and registration of tiratricol in India, which could help start generic production in a few years.
Article Summary: The drug, tiratricol, is going to be compounded by Transvaal Pharmacy for 1.8 euro per capsule. It is 99 times cheaper than the commercial drug sold by the Swedish company Egetis in Germany for 180 euro per tablet. The seven children suffer from a rare disease, Allan Herndon-Dudley Syndrome.

Around 10 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel were feared missing after two boats allegedly capsized during an operation to rescue stranded fishermen in Bethupalli lake in Telangana's Khammam district on Wednesday evening.According to news agency PTI, the personnel were conducting a rescue operation in two boats in the swollen lake, located in Sathupalli mandal, when the boats were suspected to have capsized. Article Title: TFR down, need relook at popn control laws like 2-child norm for polls: SC

NEW DELHI: Observing that laws aimed at controlling population growth in the country had lost their significance because of a fall in the total fertility rate (TFR) from 3 to 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1, Supreme Court Wednesday said the foundation of such laws had "crumbled", they had become "counter-productive" and their validity, which was upheld by it two decades ago, needed to be re-examined in the present situation.The court then decided to review its 2003 verdict for disqualifying individuals with more than two children from contesting elections to panchayati raj institutions.A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the earlier perception that population had a negative impact on development did not hold anymore, and not keeping the law abreast of changing times would have consequences far beyond the specific precedent or the law in question."Even though India's population is not yet declining, the TFR falling below the replacement rate will soon result in a demographic transition towards an older population with a declining share of the working-age population. Laws aimed at limiting population growth have now lost significance. If we fail to take note of such demographic changes, India will face serious consequences...," it said. Disqualification provisions on the basis of more than two children for local body polls have been in effect in various states. The court passed the order while examining the validity of a Maharashtra law which was challenged by a woman sarpanch. The court allowed her to hold the post despite the disqualification provision and referred the issue to a larger bench.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says laws aimed at controlling population growth have lost significance. Fall in total fertility rate (TFR) from 3 to 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1. Court then decides to review 2003 verdict for disqualifying individuals with more than two children from contesting elections.

Article Title: SC: Can't become third chamber of Parliament

'Can't interfere in norms for SC/ST seats in house'

NEW DELHI: Refusing to blur the constitutional 'Lakshman Rekha' that separates the three organs of governance, Supreme Court Wednesday said it cannot usurp legislature's exclusive powers to interfere in the criteria for reserving an assembly or parliamentary constituency for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes."We cannot become the third chamber of Parliament," a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while refusing to entertain a petition seeking quashing of a notification reserving Kadipur assembly constituency in UP for SCs.The CJI-led bench said identification of constituencies to reserve them for SCs or STs was the sole prerogative of the legislature and the court could not interfere in it, and suggested the petitioner could resort to protests to make elected representatives take corrective measures.The bench, which has been dealing with a large number of petitions on CJP protests, said in a lighter vein, "It is a good season for protest, dharna and 'naare baji'. You can also raise your voice (in protest) and tell the elected representatives that time is ripe for revising the criteria of reserving constituencies for the SC community and adopt the principle of rotational reservation. By approaching the constitutional court, you have dialled a wrong number.Appearing for a petitioner, senior advocate Gagan Gupta questioned the manner in which constituencies were geographically identified and reserved for SCs and asked whether "Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, can constitutionally operate in a manner which permits the same territorial constituencies to remain reserved for SCs over successive electoral cycles without any mechanism for periodic rotation".The bench said, "Delimitation is a legislative exercise and the guidelines for carrying out that exercise cannot be tweaked by the courts. Can the judiciary mandate the Delimitation Commission to adopt rotational reservation policy while demarcating constituencies for SCs?"The SC agreed with Allahabad HC, which had said that since Articles 330 and 332 provide for reserving constituencies for SCs and STs, no general candidate could claim that his right to contest from constituencies reserved for SCs and STs was violated.
Article Summary: The CJI-led bench said identification of constituencies to reserve them for SCs or STs was the sole prerogative of the legislature and the court could not interfere in it. The bench suggested the petitioner could resort to protests to make elected representatives take corrective measures.

Article Title: Prez can be prosecuted after leaving office but not ECs, says petitioner
Article Text:

The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, with a pending plea raising a similar issue. The provision bars courts from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against serving or former CECs and election commissioners for acts done or purported to be done in discharge of official duties.A bench told lawyers for Manoj Jha and Arun Agrawal that the cases would be tagged with the pending matter.Jha's plea argues that Section 16 gives officials wider protection than President, MPs, and SC and HC judges, covering civil and criminal proceedings during tenure and for life, without exceptions for corruption, mala fides or crime. It says President may be prosecuted after leaving office, while a former election commissioner arguably cannot."A member of Parliament who takes a bribe to vote can be tried but an EC who takes a bribe while "purporting" to act in office arguably cannot. A sitting judge of this court can be prosecuted with sanction yet a retired election commissioner cannot be prosecuted with or without it. The Constitution places no functionary above the law, however Section 16 of the CEC does," the plea said.Agrawal's plea said the wording "is or was" creates lifelong immunity, while "purporting to act" could cover conduct outside lawful authority. It said the provision contained no good-faith condition and could bar prosecution for corruption, forgery and other serious offences.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. A bench told lawyers for Manoj Jha and Arun Agrawal that the cases would be tagged with the pending matter.
